title: IonQ Completes Acquisition of SkyWater Technology, Establishing Vertically Integrated Quantum Platform - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ closed its acquisition of SkyWater Technology on July 31, 2026, paying $15.00 cash plus 0.4883 IonQ shares per SkyWater share, and becomes a vertically integrated quantum company owning design, wafer fabrication, advanced packaging and system deployment. SkyWater continues as a wholly owned subsidiary retaining its DMEA Category 1A Trusted Foundry status for defense customers.

insights.claim: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) completed its acquisition of SkyWater Technology (NASDAQ: SKYT), the largest exclusively U.S.-based semiconductor foundry, with the transaction closing on July 31, 2026 after final regulatory approvals.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A pure-play quantum hardware developer now owns a merchant foundry — model the combined cost base and foundry revenue into IONQ estimates.
insights.locator: Opening paragraph — 'Trapped-ion quantum computing developer IonQ...'

insights.claim: SkyWater shareholders received $15.00 in cash plus 0.4883 shares of IonQ common stock for each SkyWater share held at closing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The stock component sets the share-count dilution and creates a block of new IONQ holders whose cost basis is tied to the exchange ratio.
insights.quote: SkyWater shareholders received $15.00 in cash and 0.4883 shares of IonQ common stock for each share of SkyWater common stock held at closing.
insights.locator: 'Under the financial terms of the agreement...'

themes.theme: Subsidiary Structure and Trusted Foundry Status

insights.claim: SkyWater will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of IonQ under the SkyWater name, led by CEO Thomas Sonderman reporting directly to IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Retaining the SkyWater brand and management signals the foundry customer book is meant to be preserved, not absorbed.
insights.locator: 'Under the financial terms of the agreement...'

insights.claim: The SkyWater subsidiary will maintain its pure-play, DMEA Category 1A Trusted Foundry model serving existing defense and commercial customers from facilities in Minnesota, Florida and Texas.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Trusted Foundry accreditation is a defense-procurement moat that survives the deal — watch whether DoD customers stay through the ownership change.

themes.theme: Onshore Supply Chain for Fault-Tolerance Roadmap

insights.claim: Integrating SkyWater's semiconductor manufacturing directly into its supply chain is intended to accelerate IonQ's fault-tolerant quantum computing roadmap while securing an onshore supply chain for next-generation trapped-ion QPUs, quantum sensing products and quantum networking hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vertical integration is the stated mechanism for roadmap acceleration — measure it against announced QPU milestone dates, not press-release language.

insights.claim: The combined IonQ-SkyWater company will hold its Q2 2026 earnings call on August 5, 2026 after market close, followed by an investor day on September 8, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Two dated catalysts within six weeks of close — the first look at combined financials and the first post-deal strategic framing.
insights.locator: 'The combined company will host its Q2 2026 financial earnings call...'
